aliasDecisions.reason: Autumn is not an hour/time compound. Entry-wide matching through the earlier 時 target cannot establish the 秋/あき sense.

House/home in the いえ reading is distinct from the earlier うち home expression and kanji component. Teach a physical house example. The later reverse-side 裏/うら candidate also differs from the house sense. The later 内 (うち) record teaches inside a space; retain the separately contextualised 家 reading and sense.
The standalone picture word 絵/え is not established by an earlier が reading component. This is a distinct headword reading.
Standalone paper 紙/かみ is not established by earlier し component or compound readings.
Nine in the く reading is needed for 九月; earlier きゅう or deictic kana readings do not teach this pronunciation.
こっち is casual this-way, while こちら is the earlier polite expression. Count related register forms, not separate lexical senses.
先/さき ahead/before others is not equivalent to 前/まえ or the earlier future sense of 先/せん.
Four in the し reading is needed for 四月. Earlier よん and unrelated し kana readings cannot establish that reading.
Seven in the しち reading contrasts with earlier なな; count reading forms rather than new numerical senses.
背/せい in stature is a reading variant of earlier 背/せ, explicitly used with tall. Not a separate lexical sense.
Outside 外/そと is not a door word と. Broad homonym entry overlap does not teach the outside sense.
Sky 空/そら contrasts with empty 空/から. Explicitly separate the selected reading and meaning.
First day 一日/ついたち differs from one-day 一日/いちにち. These are related written forms with different readings and uses.
Sliding door 戸/と is related to earlier generic door teaching but explicitly gives this written form; not a new independent sense.
Native-series ten とお differs from earlier じゅう. Source parenthetical annotation is not part of its pronounced reading.
Teeth 歯/は are not the topic particle は/わ or an unrelated component reading. Teach the lexical ha reading.
The same spelling has outside そと and other ほか readings; each example explicitly teaches its different use. Do not count these as two distinct written headwords.
Other 外/ほか differs from outside 外/そと and the earlier door word; example states an alternative shop. Usually written ほか/他.
Gate 門/もん and room sliding door 戸/と are related opening words with distinct headword readings and contextual examples. Broad dictionary IDs do not erase this useful distinction.
Gate 門/もん is not a door と pronunciation; overlapping dictionary entries do not establish this written headword.
Easy 易しい contrasts with kind 優しい. Same kana and broad entry overlap must not conflate their meanings.
Night 夜/よる is a different reading from prior 夜/よ; teach ordinary standalone night use.
Formal modest 私/わたくし contrasts with earlier 私/わたし. Keep context formal; count register/reading forms, not independent senses.
